items.author: Óscar Calles
items.title: Venezuela welcomes opposition leader María Corina Machado home
items.summary: Venezuela’s Nobel laureate María Corina Machado returned to Caracas in a massive celebration after months in hiding and exile, sparking deep hope and sharp questions about the country’s political future.

items.author: Global Voices
items.title: Global Voices condemns the attacks on Albanian fact-checking service Faktoje
items.summary: We stand in solidarity with Faktoje following a series of coordinated attacks that have weaponized its transparent financial data to undermine its vital work exposing misinformation around local protests.

items.author: Rebecca MacKinnon
items.title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
items.summary: October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority.

items.author: Lina Ma
items.title: Unmarried Chinese women are rewriting the marriage script
items.summary: Some unmarried Chinese women are actively challenging the social stigma associated with being “leftover women” by questioning family pressure, sharing ways to escape it, or reframing the discussion altogether.

items.author: Cheryl Warner
items.title: NASA Announces X-70 Experimental Aircraft to Advance Flight Research
items.summary: On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. items.title: The scandals and suspects surrounding Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the Brazilian press
items.summary: The former president's eldest son, Flávio, had been linked to embezzlement charges in his own cabinet. During the campaign, however, his resume was exposed even further

items.author: Zulker Naeen
items.title: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
items.summary: Bangladeshi men paid agents for Russian jobs and ended up on the front lines. Families wait for bodies and answers, and they want the recruiters behind it in a courtroom.

items.author: Walid El Houri
items.title: Egypt’s crackdown on independent media reaches Mada Masr as editor faces trial
items.summary: Egypt has convicted Mada Masr’s editor-in-chief Lina Attalah and ordered the outlet closed, weeks after arresting the whole Matsada2sh newsroom.

items.author: Oiwan Lam
items.title: Unpacking Hong Kong’s rule of law score according to the World Justice Project’s ranking
items.summary: Institutional injustice, such as political nepotism, legal discrimination, and cronyism, is a far worse abusive use of power that creates systematic injustice.

items.author: Nurbek Bekmurzaev
items.title: In Kosovo, a new app makes reporting problems to the government fast and easy
items.summary: Based on the type and location of the problem, the platform is designed to route the report to the appropriate department and allow the citizen to follow what happens afterwards.

items.author: Civic Media Observatory
items.title: The Brazilian left’s quest to ‘tame’ Meta: A narrative of denouncement and resistance
items.summary: In our October edition of Undertones, we examine a movement calling for accountability and coordinated online action to challenge Meta’s problematic content moderation policies and governance practices in Brazil.
